points: Rabbi Motzen goes back to give a simple overview of both perakim 32 and 33, since he merged them the day before.
Perek 32: during the siege, Yirmiyahu is in jail, and Hashem tells him his relative Chanamel will offer to sell him the family field. It happens, and he buys it publicly through Baruch ben Neriah.
Rav David Tzvi Hoffmann says this sign was the first time Yirmiyahu felt fully sure his messages were from Hashem. Yirmiyahu asks why buy a field now, and Hashem answers: because you will come back.
Perek 33: there will be joy again, kol sasson v'kol simcha, and the kehunah and malchus that the people scorned will be rebuilt in a pure way.
One bris remains wherever we are, even without kings or Kohanim: the Torah. That's what Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai saw with "Give me Yavneh and its sages."
